page: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM per physical or virtual core. The server configuration bundles 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage alongside high block storage performance. The system does not feature hardware acceleration, operating with a GPU count of zero.

Hardware resource distribution prioritizes large memory allocations paired directly with high-capacity local temporary storage. The integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD drive delivers fast local I/O for temporary data, spillover, or caching layers without relying solely on remote volumes. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-per-core density minimizes the virtual machine footprint needed to host memory-intensive engines, optimizing hardware utilization. The configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, utilizing internal network interfaces instead.

Without integrated GPUs, the instance is not suited for hardware-accelerated deep learning or graphics rendering tasks. Instead, the combination of 32 dedicated Intel vCPUs, 256.0 GB RAM, and local NVMe storage positions the E32bds_v6 for large relational and in-memory databases, data analytics, ETL pipelines, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density alongside fast scratch storage.
